Rule Contents: If code is called dynamically and appears unused, a comment must be inserted explaining the dynamic usage.
All dead code must be deleted from the program.
Dead code includes unreachable statements, such as instructions located after a LEAVE statement, and must be removed.
Dead code is not allowed. Any FORM…ENDFORM or code block that is never called statically or dynamically must not exist.
ABAP programs must be delivered only after executing the Pretty Printer.
ABAP keywords must be in uppercase as per Pretty Printer settings.
If a DATA statement is used dynamically, a comment must be added to mention that it is accessed dynamically.
There must be no unused DATA statements in the program.
More than four nested IF…ENDIF blocks must not be used in the same program.
There should not be more than six nested FORM calls in a program.
There should not be more than four nested ENDIF statements.
When using READ TABLE with the option TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS, the INTO clause must not be used.
To reduce maintenance cost and for background programs, the function module BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT must be used.
Insert, delete, update, or modify operations on Z* tables must be followed by COMMIT WORK and ROLLBACK, except inside a user-exit.
A mass update program must have an integer parameter defining the commit frequency (package size).
A checkbox parameter for test mode must exist and its default value must be checked.
In test mode, no COMMIT must be executed.
Execution of the program must be controlled using authorization objects.
Program execution must be logged, including selection screen values, number of impacted lines, user who launched the report, and execution date/time.
The output of the test mode should be sufficient to validate whether the action will be managed correctly.
The ratio between code and comments must be at least 5%.
C-Calls, RFCExec, or SYSTEM calls must not be used.
The SQL statement CLIENT SPECIFIC must not be used.
The function module Z_CALL_SYSTEM_UNIX must not be used in new programs; its usage is tolerated only for legacy programs.
Native SQL should not be used; only Open SQL should be used. Exceptions are allowed only for specific Oracle monitoring or content server tools (e.g. DB size, content server usage).
The STOP statement must be used only in executable programs.
The STOP statement must be used only in AT SELECTION-SCREEN (without additions), START-OF-SELECTION, or GET event blocks.
The message number (SE91) referenced by MESSAGE ID mid TYPE mtype NUMBER num must exist in the message class.
Subroutine calls must have the same number of parameters and matching parameter types.
When using CALL FUNCTION, all mandatory parameters (IMPORTING, EXPORTING, TABLES) must be passed.
USING parameter in FORM must not be passed as CHANGING in PERFORM.
The usage of global variables should be very limited in terms of number.
A global variable must not be passed as an argument in a PERFORM and changed directly in the FORM at the same time.
BREAK-POINT statements must not be used outside the development system.
Within a DO…ENDDO statement, iteration disruption must be done using the EXIT statement.
Within a DO…ENDDO statement, iteration disruption must not be done using CHECK.
Data declarations must not use hyphens (e.g. DATA MY-DATA); underscores must be used instead.
Data declarations must not contain special characters such as %, $, or &.
CALL FUNCTION STARTING A NEW TASK must be used only if the function module is declared as Remote-Enabled.
When calling a function module IN BACKGROUND TASK, IN UPDATE TASK, or STARTING A NEW TASK, the EXCEPTION statement must not be used.
After a CASE statement, the first statement must be WHEN.
The last statement in a CASE block must be WHEN OTHERS to avoid dumps when an unplanned value is encountered.
When using CALL TRANSACTION, the transaction must exist; its existence can be verified using SE93.
Since NetWeaver 7.4, CALL TRANSACTION must be used with the addition WITH AUTHORITY-CHECK, as calls without authority checks are obsolete.
Before using FOR ALL ENTRIES, it must be ensured that the internal table is not empty.
